content:
Maya Chen: FYI ran the FP8 kernel canary on H100 + L40S for atlas-13b with AWQ/GPTQ variants. Short contexts look fine but long-prefix (2k-6k) evals show consistent degradation in factual QA tasks.
Sam Patel: how big is the delta?
Maya Chen: about 0.9-1.3% absolute accuracy drop on our longprefix QA set. Perplexity up ~4% on long tails. Shortctx (<512) negligible.
Diego Ruiz: that sounds like the tiling/kv-handshake issue we saw last quarter. Any NaNs or inf logs?
Maya Chen: no NaNs. Logs show subtle reordering in runqueue when mixed-precision path engages. snippet:
```
[2026-03-20T10:12:21Z] kernel: fp8_gemm_v2 launch
[2026-03-20T10:12:21Z] kv_cache: attach sequence 0x7f -> tiled
[2026-03-20T10:12:21Z] runqueue: preempt fusion flag true
[2026-03-20T10:12:21Z] result: numeric drift ~1.2e-3
```
Nia Gomez: is this reproducible on both HW types? H100 vs L40S?
Maya Chen: repro on both, slightly worse on L40S for >4k prefixes. H100 shows more variance but same directionality.
Arun Venkataraman: did you compare AWQ vs GPTQ quantization quality? Maybe AWQ interacts differently with per-channel scaling.
Maya Chen: yes. GPTQ (8-bit groupwise) had smaller drop (~0.5%), AWQ + FP8 path shows 0.9-1.3%. So there's an interaction between AWQ scale heuristics and our fp8 kernel tiling.
Sam Patel: any difference when we disable continuous batching or prefix KV caching?
Maya Chen: disabling prefix caching eliminates the regression, but latency/throughput tank. So it's a caching+tiling handshake bug, not purely quant noise.
Diego Ruiz: can you paste the canary test config?
Maya Chen: sure:
```
model: atlas-13b
quant: awq+fp8_enable=true
hw: [h100, l40s]
ctxs: [128, 1024, 2048, 4096, 6144]
batching: continuous
prefix_cache: enabled
metrics: longprefix_qa, ppl_longtail
```
canary-bot: Canary run 1774056789 -> finished. 100/100 shards. regression flagged.
devops-bot: Canary deployed to h100-pool-3 and l40s-pool-1. Rollout paused.
Nia Gomez: actionable options:
- revert fp8 kernel on longprefix route only
- force fallback to GPTQ/INT8 for routes with ctx > 2k
- patch kernel handshake (likely tiling index off-by-one in KV attach)
Arun Venkataraman: propose soft-fallback: if cache attach > N tokens then route to gpqt quant path. That keeps perf for common cases, avoids rollback.
Sam Patel: can we add a small synthetic test that exercises the fusion handoff deterministically? Need a unit we'd run in CI.
Diego Ruiz: I'll write a trace that simulates tiled kv attach + mixed-precision GEMM ordering. If we can reproduce with a tiny seq we can bisect kernel change.
Maya Chen: thanks. immediate plan: 1) abort wider rollout 2) add synthetic reproducer 3) run AWQ vs GPTQ ablation with caching off/on 4) attempt kernel patch candidate for tiling index.
Sam Patel: tagging @diego @arun to pick up kernel bisect. Nia will own rollback route and policy.
Nia Gomez: will open an ops ticket and set canary flags to disable fp8 on routes with ctx>2048.
Arun Venkataraman: also worth testing quantization scale clamping in AWQ: small clamp change reduced longprefix sensitivity in local repro.
Maya Chen: cool. I'll attach the failing examples and evaluation logs to the ticket. if anyone wants the binary to repro locally ping me.
Sam Patel: :thumbsup: keep notes short in the ticket, but include exact seeds and prompt lengths.
Maya Chen: will do.
